user: Why was the line from the external grid outside its limit for longer on 6 January than on 5 January?

grid.name: PGLib IEEE 30-Bus System (Alsac–Stott)
grid.description: Synthetic 7-day profile generated from the bundled PGLib IEEE 30-bus (Alsac–Stott) MATPOWER case: five dispatchable units with their own costs, line ratings from PGLib.

args.symptom: Bus_0 -> Bus_1 [L0] exceeded its 100% thermal limit for longer on 2000-01-06 than on 2000-01-05

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher demand near Bus_0 -> Bus_1 [L0] caused most of the increase in exceedance duration/severity.
hypotheses.finding: The window comparison attributed 18.003 %·h, or 62.9% of the 28.641 %·h increase, to demand near the line.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher demand elsewhere in the grid also increased the line's exceedance.
hypotheses.finding: Demand elsewhere contributed 6.801 %·h (23.7%) of the increase; it amplified with nearby demand.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Changes in generator output contributed to the longer exceedance.
hypotheses.finding: Units' output contributed 3.837 %·h, or 13.4% of the increase.

result.message: Over 2000-01-06 00:00 to 2000-01-06 23:45, Bus_0 -> Bus_1 [L0] has 37.7 %·h outside its limits; over 2000-01-05 00:00 to 2000-01-05 23:45 (the window asked for) it had 9.1 %·h outside its limits. Of the 28.6 %·h rise: Demand near Bus_0 -> Bus_1 [L0] 63 %; Demand elsewhere 24 %; Units' output 13 %. Demand near Bus_0 -> Bus_1 [L0] and demand elsewhere amplify each other (+28 % of the change comes from the two together).

classical.not_applicable: The classical views are computed for one moment, not over a window; investigate a moment of the window to see them.

result.method: Every combination of the factors, each at its value now or in the reference state, was solved by AC power flow. A factor's share is its Shapley value — its average effect over every order in which the changes could have happened — so the shares add up to the change, interactions included. Over a window, every combination solves every moment pair.

load_power_factor.applies_to: measured loads (Q = P·tan(acos pf)); the nominal point keeps the case's own Q

assistant:
The external-grid connection is **Bus_0 → Bus_1 [L0]**. It exceeded the 100% line-loading limit for **2.50 hours (10 ticks)** on 6 January, versus **1.25 hours (5 ticks)** on 5 January. Its total exceedance severity was **37.7 %·h** versus **9.1 %·h**.

The comparison attributes the increase mainly to **demand near the line** (62.9% of the increase). **Demand elsewhere** contributed another 23.7%, and **changes in unit output** contributed 13.4%. Nearby and wider-area demand amplified each other, accounting for 28.5% of the increase through their interaction.

📋 Data source: measurements.
